I have farmed this small piece of land since I was a young girl, and I know every part of it. It is only 0.17 hectares, and I grow cassava and beans there together. I will not buy chemical fertilizer from the shop because one bag costs too many shillings and is more than this little plot needs. Instead, I will carry two buckets of manure from the goats behind my house and spread it with my hands before planting. I will use the same cassava sticks I saved from last season and the beans I kept from the harvest before — not the new seeds from the shop, because those cost money and I have not seen them do better on my neighbor's plot. I do not spray anything, and I cannot carry water to irrigate, so I wait for the rains like always. I will work there myself on the days my legs are strong, and my grandchildren help with the hoe when they are home. All together we will spend about 20 days on this plot clearing, planting, weeding, and digging. I will not hire outside workers because I do not have cash to pay them.
